Question for you: the whole-article check points out that your addition has the community weighing in on a member's social media and ChatGPT. Later the essay says there's a floor the majority can't vote away, and it includes "private thought, contact with people outside the community". I don't think they clash: the floor protects contact with outsiders, not any one app, and your addition argues both sides. But a reader could take it as the community deciding what apps adults use. Leave it, or add a few words of your own?
A fresh reader also noticed a jump from personal apps in P5 to whole institutions in P6 (banking, schools and so on). I'd leave it: P6 widens the question on purpose.
